P-ELS.summary: Authors may use AI tools to support manuscript preparation with human oversight and must include a separate AI declaration in the manuscript, except for basic grammar/spelling checks and disability-related assistive uses. AI cannot be an author, and AI images are allowed only for explanatory figures, data-derived visualizations, and approved cover art; primary research images and graphical abstracts from general-purpose generative AI are not allowed. Reviewers and editors may use AI only in a supportive capacity with private tools and must never upload manuscript content; reviewers must disclose their AI use.

evidence.quote: Authors preparing a manuscript for an Elsevier journal can use AI tools to support them in these tasks.
Basic checks of grammar, spelling and punctuation do not need a declaration statement.
Authors should not list AI tools as an author or co-author, nor cite AI tools as an author.
AI tools must not be used to create or alter images that represent primary observed or experimental data
AI tools may therefore only be used in a supportive capacity, for example to improve the language and structure of a review report
Reviewers should not upload a submitted manuscript or any part of it into an AI tool
Editors may therefore only use AI tools in a supportive capacity, for example to improve the language or structure of their decision letters

P-WIL.summary: Wiley welcomes responsible author use of AI as a companion to writing, provided authors stay fully accountable, check tool terms for rights, and disclose substantive uses (text generation, methodology, visuals) but not simple grammar or formatting help. AI cannot be an author, and AI-edited photographs and factual or evidential images are not permitted. Reviewers and editors may use AI only for things like polishing feedback, must never upload manuscripts (even in part), and reviewers must disclose AI used for drafting reviews.

evidence.quote: Wiley welcomes the thoughtful use of AI Technology.
Simple grammar correction, formatting, and word choice suggestions typically do not require disclosure.
these tools cannot fulfil the role of, nor be listed as, an author of an article.
AI-edited photographs are not permitted in Wiley journals.
Manuscripts under review are confidential and must not be uploaded to AI Technologies, whether in full or in part.
Use AI to improve review clarity and tone or translate your review
What editors and reviewers can do safely:

P-SAG.summary: Sage separates assistive AI use (language, grammar, structure), which needs no disclosure, from generative AI use that affects content, methods, results or images, which must be disclosed and verified by authors. Reviewers may use AI for help writing and formatting reports but must not upload manuscripts or have AI generate their reviews. Editors must not use GenAI for editorial work such as decision letters or summaries of unpublished research.

evidence.quote: are considered assistive AI tools and do not require disclosure by authors or reviewers.
must be disclosed upon submission so the editorial team can evaluate the content generated.
Generated images that are presented as unique or novel research images
Generation of representative illustrations or infographics
Peer reviewers may use generative AI (GenAI) to help write and format the peer review reports
such as uploading or copy-pasting the manuscript or parts of it to a GenAI tool
Editors must not use ChatGPT or other GenAI to generate decision letters, or summaries of unpublished research.

P-OUP.summary: Authors may use generative AI tools when preparing manuscripts. Basic language correction and reference formatting need no disclosure, while substantial editing, translation, data analysis, code, and illustrative images must be disclosed. Fabricating research data or creating/altering primary scientific images is not allowed, and non-disclosure may lead to rejection, correction, or retraction.

evidence.quote: This policy explains how authors may use generative AI tools (Gen AI Tools) when preparing manuscripts for OUP journals
Improving clarity of language (e.g. spelling or grammar correction)
Any use of Gen AI Tools should be disclosed both in your cover letter to editors and in the Acknowledgements section of manuscripts.
Generating illustrative or explanatory images, such as graphical abstracts, using AI
Creating or altering primary factual, scientific, or technical images, such as clinical or diagnostic images

P-SPR.summary: Springer Nature uses a green/amber/red risk framework for AI across authors, reviewers and editors. Low-risk assistive use (e.g. language polishing) is permitted, higher-risk evaluative use needs human oversight and disclosure, and opaque use, fabrication, AI authorship, delegating peer review to AI, and photorealistic deepfake images are not permitted. Reviewers may use AI to support review but must not upload manuscript content to unsecured or public AI tools.

evidence.quote: Permitted with human oversight, verification, and transparency through disclosure.
Disclose AI use for trust and transparency
Assigning authorship or accountability to AI systems or tools
Creating photorealistic images (deepfakes)
May use AI to support peer review but must not upload manuscript content to unsecured or public AI tools
Manuscripts, peer review reports, and sensitive data must not be shared with unsecured or public AI systems.
Apply proportional, risk‑based judgement when assessing AI use

P-EME.summary: Emerald bans using generative AI to write or generate new content, data or results, but permits AI copy-editing of the author's own work, translation, and illustrative images, with transparent declaration and human accountability. AI cannot be an author. Reviewers and editors may not use generative AI to evaluate manuscripts or upload files to AI tools, though reviewers may use it to copy-edit their review reports and must declare this.

evidence.quote: Copywriting (creating, drafting, or writing) any part of a submission using generative AI tools and technology to generate new material is not permitted.
Copy-editing (correcting, editing, formatting, modifying, or refining) all or part of an author’s own original existing work using generative AI tools and technology
must be flagged, clearly and transparently, by authors within the Methods and Acknowledgements (or another appropriate section) of the work.
LLMs cannot be credited with authorship as they do not have legal standing or the ability to assign copyright
Purpose is here defined as either illustrative, which is permitted, or factual/evidential, which is not permitted.
Reviewers may, however, use a generative AI tool to copy-edit and improve the quality of the language in their review
Any work or files submitted to Emerald for consideration and review should not be uploaded to a generative AI tool or Large Language Model (LLM).
Emerald does not permit the use of generative AI tools or LLMs to assist in the review, evaluation, or decision-making process

P-TF.summary: Taylor & Francis permits authors to use generative AI responsibly for tasks like idea generation, copyediting, translation, literature classification and coding help, provided they review outputs, disclose the tool, version, how and why it was used, and never list AI as an author. AI may help with data visualisations and conceptual illustrations but not create or manipulate research results or clinical/diagnostic images. Editors and peer reviewers must not upload unpublished manuscripts into AI tools; reviewers may only use AI to improve the language of their reports, and editors should check with T&F before using any tool.

evidence.quote: Taylor & Francis supports the responsible use of Generative AI tools that respect high standards of data security, confidentiality, and copyright protection
Authors must clearly acknowledge within the article or book any use of Generative AI tools
Generative AI tools must not be listed as an author
does not permit the use of Generative AI in the creation or manipulation of outputs of research or clinical testing
Generative AI may be utilised to assist with improving review language.
peer reviewers must not upload unpublished manuscripts or project proposals, including any associated files, images, or information, into Generative AI tools.
Editors should check with their Taylor & Francis contact prior to using any Generative AI tools

P-INF.summary: INFORMS permits authors to use generative AI when preparing manuscripts, but AI/ML tools cannot be listed as authors and authors remain fully responsible for the accuracy and originality of the work. Any AI use must be disclosed in the acknowledgements with the tool and the nature of assistance, and references (especially AI-generated ones) must be verified against original sources. The page does not address AI use by reviewers or editors, or AI-generated images.

evidence.quote: Authors are permitted to use generative artificial intelligence (AI) in the preparation of their manuscripts.
machine learning (ML) and AI tools may not be listed as authors.
must be disclosed in the acknowledgements section, with details of the tool used and the nature of the assistance provided.

P-AOM.summary: Authors may use AI tools but must disclose use at each research stage, confirm they verified all AI output, and note language model use in the cover letter and acknowledgements (or title page for Annual Meeting submissions). Reviewers must not upload any manuscript material to AI tools and may use AI only to polish their own reviews, though another passage says they must not use AI to generate review reports. Editors must not share manuscript or review information with generative AI.

evidence.quote: Authors may use AI tools in their research, but AI cannot replace human judgment or accountability at any stage
For each stage of the research process, authors must identify whether AI tools were used
Reviewers should not upload any portion of a manuscript, including text, figures, or data, into any AI tool or platform.
Reviewers may, however, use AI tools to assist in editing or improving the clarity of their own written reviews.
Editors must not share information about submitted manuscripts or peer review reports with generative AI or LLMs such as ChatGPT.
Presentation of Results — Creating tables, figures, or other visual representations.

P-AEA.summary: AI tools such as chatbots cannot be listed as authors. Authors who use AI in preparing a manuscript, including drafting or editing text, must briefly describe that use during submission and are fully accountable for fact-checking AI outputs. Reviewers must base their reports on their own reading, may use only AI tools that guarantee manuscripts are not used for training, and must disclose any use in their cover letter.

evidence.quote: may not be listed as an author
this must be briefly described during the submission process
Authors are solely accountable for, and must thoroughly fact-check, outputs created with the help of AI software.
Any use of AI during the review must be disclosed in the reviewer's cover letter
must be limited to tools that guarantee that the manuscript will not be used for training AI models

P-APA.summary: APA allows authors to use generative AI tools when drafting manuscripts, provided the use is disclosed in the manuscript and cited, and authors verify all AI-provided information and citations. AI cannot be listed as an author. Submitted content must not be entered into generative AI tools because doing so breaches confidentiality of the review process.

evidence.quote: the use of AI **must** be disclosed in the manuscript and [cited]
AI **cannot** be named as an author on an APA scholarly publication.
Authors may use but must disclose AI tools for specific purposes such as editing.
No submitted content may be entered into generative AI tools as this violates the confidentiality of the process.

P-AAA.summary: Authors may use generative AI and AI-assisted tools if they disclose the specific tools and uses and keep human oversight, taking full responsibility for the content. Disclosure goes in the methodology for research design/analysis, or in a dedicated declaration before the references for other uses; basic spelling/grammar checkers and reference managers need no disclosure. AI cannot be listed as an author, and AI creation or alteration of images is prohibited unless it is part of the research design or methods. This authors-only policy does not set rules for reviewers or editors' use of AI.

evidence.quote: authors may use generative AI and AI-assisted tools to assist with the generation of scholarly work
as long as they disclose the specific use(s) of the tool and the tool(s) used
use of spelling and grammar checking tools and reference manager tools, which may rely on AI or AI-assisted technologies does not require disclosure
Authors should not list AI or AI-assisted tools as an author or co-author
We do not permit the use of AI or AI-assisted tools to create or alter images in submitted manuscripts.

S-AMA.summary: The AMA page defers its generative AI policy to Sage Publications' AI policy and gives no author-facing AI rules itself. The only explicit AI rule on the page is that review team members may not enter any part of a manuscript into generative AI.

evidence.quote: Review team members are prohibited from entering any part of the manuscript into generative AI.
Review team members are prohibited from entering any part of the manuscript into generative AI.

S-ECTA.summary: Authors may use AI tools when preparing Econometrica manuscripts but remain fully accountable for all content, including verifying AI output and protecting data privacy and IP. AI software cannot be listed as an author. The journals themselves use the AI tool Refine on conditionally accepted papers to flag technical and expository issues, without training AI models on manuscripts.

evidence.quote: Authors preparing a manuscript for Econometrica may use AI tools, but remain responsible and accountable for all content of their work.
AI software, such as chatbots or other large language models, may not be listed as an author.
The journals of the ES will conduct checks on conditionally accepted papers using the AI tool Refine.

J-MNSC.summary: Management Science says it cannot stop authors from using generative AI, but authors remain fully responsible for accuracy, and submitting a manuscript counts as a declaration that they reviewed and edited any AI-generated content. Members of the review team (reviewers and editors) must make their conclusions their own and are responsible for their accuracy. They must not upload manuscript content into generative AI tools in a way that could compromise confidentiality or copyright. No disclosure requirement, AI authorship rule, or AI image rule is stated.

evidence.quote: We cannot prevent authors from using generative AI in the preparation of their manuscripts.
submission of a manuscript is taken as a declaration that the author(s) reviewed and edited any AI-generated content as needed
All conclusions expressed by each member of the review team (reviewers, Associate Editor, Department Editor) should be theirs and theirs only.
should not upload any part of a manuscript submitted to Management Science into a generative AI tool such that it might compromise confidentiality
The author of any review is responsible for the accuracy of all conclusions and references cited.

J-MKSC.summary: Authors are welcome to use generative AI tools when preparing manuscripts, but they remain fully responsible for the accuracy of all facts and references. Papers with errors such as hallucinated references can be rejected outright or treated as a potential ethical violation. The page does not state disclosure requirements, and reviewer and editor AI rules are only linked to a separate page, not covered here.

evidence.quote: Authors are welcome to use generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) tools in the preparation of their manuscripts.
the authors are responsible for the accuracy of all facts and references cited in the paper.

J-MSOM.summary: Authors may use generative AI when preparing manuscripts but remain fully responsible for accuracy, and submission implies they reviewed and edited any AI-generated content. Members of the review team (reviewers, Associate Editors, Department Editors) must ensure conclusions are their own and must not upload any part of a manuscript into a generative AI tool in a way that could compromise confidentiality or copyright. The page does not address disclosure, AI authorship, or AI-generated images.

submission of a manuscript is taken as a declaration that the author(s) reviewed and edited any AI-generated content as needed

should not upload any part of a manuscript submitted to Manufacturing & Service Operations Management into a generative AI tool such that it might compromise confidentiality

J-OPRE.summary: The page only covers reviewers and editors, not authors. Reviewers and editors must keep submitted manuscripts and review materials confidential and may not upload them to public-access generative AI tools, though openly posted materials (e.g., arXiv papers) may be uploaded. Privacy-preserving AI tools conforming to RELX Responsible AI Principles may be used, and reviewers and editors remain fully responsible for the accuracy and reasoning of their reports.

evidence.quote: may therefore not be uploaded to public-access generative AI technology
Materials posted openly (e.g., papers and images from papers on arXiv, SSRN, author web site, etc.) may be uploaded
AI-driven techniques that conform to the RELX Responsible AI Principles and that preserve the privacy of submitted materials may be used
The Area Editor, Associate Editor, and reviewers are all responsible for their final report, and the accuracy and reasoning therein.

J-MISQ.summary: This is a September 2023 editorial by the editor-in-chief on innovation at MIS Quarterly, not a formal AI policy. Guest sections by two board members discuss generative AI and AGI as future opportunities and say the journal may need policies later. No rules are set for authors, reviewers or editors.

J-HBR.summary: HBR acknowledges that many contributors use AI tools and asks authors to tell their editor, and note on the copyright form, whether and how they used them. Authors remain fully accountable for accuracy, integrity, sourcing and originality. Editors may use AI for their own workflows, but submissions cannot be used to train AI models and humans make all publication decisions.

evidence.quote: We understand many of our contributors use AI tools.
we ask our contributors to share whether and how they’ve used these tools with their editor and on our copyright form
our authors are accountable for the accuracy, integrity, sourcing, and originality of their content
Our editors may use AI tools to support their own editorial workflows, but we don’t allow submissions to be used to train AI models

J-SMR.summary: The Author Guidelines page now only announces that MIT Sloan Management Review is ending print publication and that a new digital version will launch. It tells interested authors to email for inquiries and contains no policy on generative AI use by authors, reviewers, or editors.
